sources.entry: VidCrop - A simple video cropping tool that supports multiple formats and precise trimming.

summary.name: VidCrop
summary.one_liner: VidCrop is a macOS video cropping utility with a built-in media player for cropping frames, trimming timelines, adjusting speed, and adding watermarks and subtitles.
use_cases: Cropping a video to a specific aspect ratio such as 9:16 for social media
Trimming the start or end of a video clip
Adding a text or image watermark to a video
Exporting a video as GIF or MP4
Slowing down or speeding up a video for export
Adding or editing subtitles on a video
summary.what_it_does: VidCrop lets you import videos by drag-and-drop or file open and preview them in a built-in player. You can drag to select a crop area or set width, height, and aspect ratios such as 1:1, 16:9, and 9:16. A filmstrip timeline with yellow handles sets In and Out trim points. It also changes playback and export speed, downscales output resolution proportionally, and adds text or avatar watermarks, either fixed or randomly floating, plus subtitle import, editing, and preview. Export formats listed are MP4, MOV, GIF, and more.
notable: Built-in media player with frame cropping and filmstrip timeline trimming
Text or avatar watermarks, fixed or randomly floating, and tiled watermarks with rotation and spacing in recent updates
Subtitle import, add, edit and preview
Localized in English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, and Chinese variants
caveats: One user reported exports taking significantly longer than Final Cut Pro for the same file, with high fan usage
Pricing is not stated on the page
